scenes.text: They're full of potassium, and a tiny part of all potassium is radioactive potassium forty.
Scientists even joke about a unit called the banana equivalent dose.
But one banana gives you about one hundredth of the radiation you get every single day.
And your body keeps its potassium level steady, so it doesn't build up.
You're actually a little radioactive yourself!
Will this change how you look at your breakfast?

title: Bananas are radioactive (and so are you) 🍌
caption: Bananas contain potassium, and a tiny fraction of potassium is radioactive potassium-40. One banana is about 0.1 microsieverts, roughly 1% of a normal day's natural background radiation. Totally safe!
